s321.content:
Callixtus began life as a slave. After a troubled youth and a sentence to the mines of Sardinia, he became a deacon in charge of the Christian burial ground on the Appian Way, which still bears his name: the Catacomb of St. Callixtus.

As pope he welcomed repentant sinners back to communion, to the anger of rigorists like Hippolytus. He was killed during a riot and is honored as a martyr.
s321.intercession: Pope St. Callixtus, pray for us. Teach the Church to welcome sinners home with mercy. Amen.

s322.content:
Pontian was bishop of Rome when the Emperor Maximinus Thrax exiled him, along with the theologian Hippolytus, to the deadly mines of Sardinia.

Knowing he would not return, he resigned his office so that the Church of Rome would not be left without a shepherd, the first pope known to do so. He died there of harsh treatment, and is honored with Hippolytus, with whom he was reconciled.
s322.intercession: Pope St. Pontian, pray for us. Teach us to put the good of the Church before ourselves. Amen.

s323.content:
Gregory was a young lawyer who came under the spell of the great teacher Origen in Caesarea and was converted to Christ. He became bishop of his home city of Neocaesarea in Pontus.

So many miracles were reported of him that he was called "the Wonderworker." Tradition says that when he became bishop there were only seventeen Christians in the city, and at his death only seventeen pagans.
s323.intercession: St. Gregory the Wonderworker, pray for us. Intercede for us in desperate situations, and help us to win others for Christ. Amen.

s324.content:
Dionysius, called "the Great," headed the famous catechetical school of Alexandria and then served as its bishop for seventeen years. He survived the persecutions of Decius and Valerian, escaping arrest and enduring exile.

His letters describe how Christians in Alexandria nursed the sick during a terrible plague, caring even for pagans who had fled their own families, and often dying themselves.
s324.intercession: St. Dionysius, pray for us. Make us generous and brave in caring for the sick. Amen.

s325.content:
Peter was bishop of Alexandria during the Great Persecution under Diocletian. He wrote rules for welcoming back Christians who had lapsed under torture, and excommunicated Arius, then a young deacon, for joining a schism.

He was beheaded in 311, one of the last victims of the persecution, and the Coptic Church calls him "the Seal of the Martyrs."
s325.intercession: St. Peter of Alexandria, pray for us. Strengthen persecuted Christians, and keep the Church faithful to the truth. Amen.

s326.content:
Methodius was a bishop and writer in Lycia, in Asia Minor. His best-known work, the Symposium, imitates Plato’s famous dialogue: ten virgins in a garden each give a speech in praise of chastity, ending with a hymn to Christ the Bridegroom.

He defended the resurrection of the body against some ideas of Origen, and tradition says he died a martyr at the end of the Great Persecution.
s326.intercession: St. Methodius, pray for us. Help us to honor our bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

s327.content:
Gregory brought the faith to Armenia. According to tradition, King Tiridates III had him thrown into a deep pit at Khor Virap, where he survived for thirteen years.

Released to heal the king of a terrible illness, he baptized him around 301, making Armenia the first nation to adopt Christianity as its official religion. He became the first head of the Armenian Church.
s327.intercession: St. Gregory the Illuminator, pray for us. Bless the Armenian people, and help us to remain faithful in long trials. Amen.

s328.content:
Sylvester became bishop of Rome in 314, just after the Emperor Constantine ended the persecution of Christians. During his long reign the great basilicas of St. John Lateran and St. Peter’s were built, and the Council of Nicaea was held in 325.

Many legends grew up around him, including the forged "Donation of Constantine." His feast falls on New Year’s Eve, which in many countries is still called "Silvester."
s328.intercession: Pope St. Sylvester, pray for us. Help the Church to use times of peace well, for the glory of God. Amen.

s329.content:
Alexander was bishop of Alexandria when one of his priests, Arius, began teaching that the Son of God was a creature who had not always existed. Alexander condemned him after patient attempts to correct him.

At the Council of Nicaea in 325 he led the defense of Christ’s full divinity, accompanied by his young deacon and secretary, St. Athanasius, who succeeded him.
s329.intercession: St. Alexander, pray for us. Keep us faithful to the true faith in Christ, God from God, Light from Light. Amen.

s330.content:
Eustathius was bishop of Antioch and one of the leading defenders of the faith at the Council of Nicaea in 325.

After the council, Arian bishops took revenge by accusing him of misconduct and having him deposed and exiled to Thrace, where he died. His loyal followers in Antioch, the "Eustathians," kept the Nicene faith for decades.
s330.intercession: St. Eustathius, pray for us. Strengthen all who are falsely accused for their faithfulness. Amen.

s331.content:
Spyridon was a married shepherd on Cyprus who became bishop of Trimythous while keeping his simple life and his flocks. Tradition places him among the bishops at the Council of Nicaea.

A beloved legend tells that he explained the Trinity to a philosopher by squeezing a brick, which burst into flame, released water, and left clay in his hand: three, yet one. His relics are venerated on the island of Corfu.
s331.intercession: St. Spyridon, pray for us. Help us to explain the mysteries of faith simply, and keep us humble in every honor. Amen.

s332.content:
Jacob was the first bishop of Nisibis, a frontier city between the Roman and Persian empires in today’s Turkey. He attended the Council of Nicaea and founded a famous school in his city.

He was the teacher of St. Ephrem the Syrian. Tradition credits his prayers with saving Nisibis from a Persian siege.
s332.intercession: St. Jacob, pray for us. Bless teachers of the faith and all Christians who live on dangerous frontiers. Amen.

s333.content:
Paul of Thebes fled into the Egyptian desert as a young man to escape the persecution of Decius, and stayed there in a cave for nearly ninety years, living on dates and water. St. Jerome wrote his life.

According to Jerome, St. Anthony the Great was led to visit him near the end of his life, and a raven that had brought Paul half a loaf each day brought a whole loaf for the two of them.
s333.intercession: St. Paul the Hermit, pray for us. Teach us to find our joy in God alone. Amen.

s334.content:
Macarius was a camel driver who became a disciple of St. Anthony and then a monk and priest in the desert of Scetis in Egypt, where communities of monks gathered around him.

He was famous for his humility and gentleness. Asked how to pray, he answered that there is no need for many words: just stretch out your hands and say, "Lord, as you will and as you know, have mercy on me."
s334.intercession: St. Macarius, pray for us. Teach us humility and the simple prayer of the heart. Amen.

s335.content:
Hilarion was born near Gaza and converted to Christianity as a student in Alexandria. After visiting St. Anthony in the desert, he returned home to live as a hermit and became the founder of monastic life in Palestine.

Crowds seeking healing kept him on the move: to Egypt, Sicily, Dalmatia, and finally Cyprus, where he died. St. Jerome wrote his life.
s335.intercession: St. Hilarion, pray for us. Help us to seek silence and prayer amid the noise of the world. Amen.

s336.content:
Frumentius was a boy from Tyre who, with his brother, was captured after their ship was attacked on the Red Sea. Brought to the court of Aksum in Ethiopia, he became the king’s secretary and tutor to the young prince.

He went to Alexandria to ask St. Athanasius for a bishop for Ethiopia, and Athanasius consecrated Frumentius himself. Ethiopians call him Abba Salama, "Father of Peace."
s336.intercession: St. Frumentius, pray for us. Bless the Church in Ethiopia, and help us to serve God wherever life takes us. Amen.

s337.content:
Nino was a Christian woman, probably from Cappadocia, who brought the faith to the kingdom of Iberia, in today’s Georgia. According to tradition, she healed the queen through prayer.

When King Mirian was saved from darkness after praying to "Nino’s God," he and his people became Christian. Her cross of grapevine branches bound with her own hair is a symbol of the Georgian Church.
s337.intercession: St. Nino, pray for us. Bless the people of Georgia, and help women who share the faith in their families and communities. Amen.

s338.content:
Julius was bishop of Rome during the bitter years after Nicaea, when Arian emperors and bishops drove the defenders of the Creed from their sees.

He welcomed the exiled St. Athanasius to Rome, declared him innocent at a synod, and firmly upheld the Nicene faith. He also built several churches in Rome.
s338.intercession: Pope St. Julius, pray for us. Help the Church to defend those who suffer for the truth. Amen.

s339.content:
Eusebius was the first bishop of Vercelli in northern Italy, and the first Western bishop known to have his clergy live together in community under a common rule of prayer.

At a council in Milan in 355, he refused to condemn St. Athanasius and was exiled by the Arian emperor to Palestine and Egypt. He returned to work for the Nicene faith in Italy.
s339.intercession: St. Eusebius, pray for us. Give priests a love of common prayer and the courage to stand for the truth. Amen.

s340.content:
Zeno, probably born in North Africa, was bishop of Verona in Italy. About ninety of his sermons survive, among the oldest Latin sermons we have, many of them preached to those preparing for Baptism at Easter.

He was known for his charity and his love of fishing, and the beautiful Romanesque basilica of San Zeno in Verona stands over his tomb.
s340.intercession: St. Zeno, pray for us. Bless the city of Verona, and help us to live the grace of our Baptism. Amen.

s341.content:
Meletius was bishop of Antioch during the Arian crisis and was sent into exile three times. A gentle and holy man, he ordained St. John Chrysostom a deacon.

He presided over the Council of Constantinople in 381, which completed the Nicene Creed, but died during the council. St. Gregory of Nyssa preached at his funeral.
s341.intercession: St. Meletius, pray for us. Bring peace to divided communities, and keep us faithful in times of confusion. Amen.

s342.content:
Optatus was bishop of Milevis in North Africa when the Church there was torn by the Donatist schism, which held that sacraments given by unworthy clergy were invalid.

In his work against the Donatists, he argued that the sacraments belong to Christ, not to the minister, and that unity with the See of Peter in Rome is the mark of the true Church. St. Augustine admired him.
s342.intercession: St. Optatus, pray for us. Heal divisions in the Church and keep us united with the successor of Peter. Amen.

s343.content:
Amphilochius was a lawyer and the cousin of St. Gregory of Nazianzus, and a close friend of St. Basil. He became bishop of Iconium and attended the Council of Constantinople in 381.

A famous story tells that he greeted the Emperor Theodosius but ignored the young prince at his side. When the emperor took offense, he replied that God the Father is offended too when men honor Him but not His Son.
s343.intercession: St. Amphilochius, pray for us. Help us to honor the Son as we honor the Father. Amen.

s344.content:
Peter was the youngest of ten children in a remarkable family of saints, brother of Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa, and Macrina, who largely raised him.

He lived for years as a monk and became bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, where he worked against Arianism and attended the Council of Constantinople in 381.
s344.intercession: St. Peter of Sebaste, pray for us. Bless families who help one another toward holiness. Amen.

s345.content:
Pacian was bishop of Barcelona and a married man before his ordination. St. Jerome praised his eloquence and holy life.

In his letters he defended the Church’s power to forgive sins through penance, against those who said some sins could never be forgiven. He is remembered for the line, "Christian is my name, Catholic my surname."
s345.intercession: St. Pacian, pray for us. Help us to bear the name of Christian and Catholic with joy, and to trust in God’s forgiveness. Amen.

s346.content:
Epiphanius was born in Palestine, became a monk, and later was bishop of Salamis on Cyprus for nearly forty years. He was said to know Hebrew, Syriac, Egyptian, Greek, and Latin.

His Panarion, or "Medicine Chest," describes and refutes eighty heresies, preserving information about many ancient groups that would otherwise be lost.
s346.intercession: St. Epiphanius, pray for us. Give us a love for the truth and the wisdom to recognize error. Amen.

s347.content:
Chromatius was bishop of Aquileia, a great city at the head of the Adriatic. A friend of St. Jerome, he encouraged Jerome’s translation of the Bible and tried to reconcile him with his former friend Rufinus.

He defended St. John Chrysostom when Chrysostom was exiled. Many of his sermons were rediscovered only in the 20th century.
s347.intercession: St. Chromatius, pray for us. Make us peacemakers between friends who are divided. Amen.

s348.content:
Gaudentius was on pilgrimage in the East when the people of Brescia chose him as their bishop. Only when the bishops of the region threatened to refuse him communion did he return to accept.

He was later sent to Constantinople to defend St. John Chrysostom and was imprisoned on the way. Twenty-one of his sermons survive.
s348.intercession: St. Gaudentius, pray for us. Help us to accept God’s call with humility, and to defend the innocent. Amen.

s349.content:
Niceta was bishop of Remesiana, in today’s Serbia, and a tireless missionary among the tribes of the Balkans. His friend St. Paulinus of Nola praised him for teaching barbarians to sing hymns to Christ.

He wrote instructions for those preparing for Baptism and encouraged singing in church. Many scholars think he may have written the Te Deum.
s349.intercession: St. Niceta, pray for us. Teach us to praise God with joy, and bless missionaries to every people. Amen.

s350.content:
Innocent was pope during the collapse of the Western Empire, and Alaric’s Goths sacked Rome in 410 while he was away pleading for peace in Ravenna.

He strengthened the authority of the Roman see, supported the exiled St. John Chrysostom, and wrote an important letter on the liturgy and the sacraments, including the anointing of the sick.
s350.intercession: Pope St. Innocent, pray for us. Guide the Church in times of upheaval and fear. Amen.

s351.content:
Maximus was the first known bishop of Turin, serving during the barbarian invasions of northern Italy. About a hundred of his sermons survive.

He urged his people to stay and defend their city, to welcome refugees, and to share their goods with the poor, and he gently rebuked those who clung to pagan customs.
s351.intercession: St. Maximus, pray for us. Make us generous to refugees and to all who are in need. Amen.

s352.content:
Ninian was a Briton who, according to St. Bede, was trained in Rome and returned to evangelize the southern Picts. At Whithorn in Galloway he built a stone church called Candida Casa, "the White House."

Whithorn became a center of learning and pilgrimage. Ninian is honored as one of the first missionaries to the land that became Scotland.
s352.intercession: St. Ninian, pray for us. Bless the people of Scotland, and give us zeal to share the Gospel. Amen.

s353.content:
Celestine was pope when the patriarch Nestorius denied that Mary could be called Mother of God. He sent legates to the Council of Ephesus in 431, which proclaimed Mary Theotokos, "God-bearer."

He also sent the deacon Palladius as the first bishop to the Christians of Ireland, preparing the way for St. Patrick.
s353.intercession: Pope St. Celestine, pray for us. Help us to honor Mary as the Mother of God. Amen.

s354.content:
John Cassian spent years among the monks of Egypt, listening to the great desert fathers. He later founded two monasteries in Marseille, in Gaul.

His Institutes and Conferences carried the wisdom of the Egyptian desert to the West. St. Benedict told his monks to read them, and they shaped Western monastic life for centuries.
s354.intercession: St. John Cassian, pray for us. Teach us to pray without ceasing and to guard our hearts. Amen.

s355.content:
Possidius was a member of St. Augustine’s community in Hippo for forty years, then bishop of nearby Calama. He shared Augustine’s battles against the Donatists and Pelagians.

He was at Augustine’s bedside in 430 as the Vandals besieged Hippo, and soon after wrote his Life of Augustine, the first biography of the great saint. The Vandals later drove him into exile.
s355.intercession: St. Possidius, pray for us. Bless faithful friends, and help us to learn from the saints we love. Amen.

s356.content:
Vincent was a monk on the island of Lérins, off the coast of Provence. In his Commonitorium, written in 434, he asked how to tell true teaching from error.

His answer became famous: hold to what has been believed everywhere, always, and by all. He also explained that doctrine truly develops, but like a body growing from childhood to adulthood, never changing into something else.
s356.intercession: St. Vincent of Lérins, pray for us. Keep us faithful to the faith of the whole Church, in every age. Amen.

s357.content:
Proclus was a disciple of St. John Chrysostom. In 428, preaching in Constantinople in front of the patriarch Nestorius, he delivered a famous sermon defending Mary’s title Mother of God.

As archbishop of Constantinople, he brought the relics of St. John Chrysostom back to the city in 438, and was known for his gentleness toward those who disagreed with him.
s357.intercession: St. Proclus, pray for us. Help us to honor Mary as the Mother of God, and to be gentle with those who disagree with us. Amen.

s358.content:
Germanus was a Roman lawyer and provincial governor who was chosen bishop of Auxerre in Gaul. He gave away his wealth and lived austerely.

In 429 he was sent to Britain to combat Pelagianism. According to tradition, he led the Britons to victory over invading Picts and Saxons by having them shout "Alleluia!" so loudly that the enemy fled.
s358.intercession: St. Germanus, pray for us. Defend the true faith, and give us confidence in the power of praise. Amen.

s359.content:
Flavian, archbishop of Constantinople, condemned the monk Eutyches for teaching that Christ had only one nature after the Incarnation. Pope St. Leo the Great wrote his famous Tome to Flavian supporting him.

At the violent "Robber Council" of Ephesus in 449, Flavian was beaten and died of his injuries in exile. The Council of Chalcedon honored him as a martyr two years later.
s359.intercession: St. Flavian, pray for us. Give us courage to confess Christ, true God and true man. Amen.

s360.content:
Hilary was a young nobleman persuaded by his relative St. Honoratus to become a monk at Lérins. He succeeded Honoratus as bishop of Arles before he was thirty.

He lived austerely, worked with his own hands, and sold the church’s silver vessels to ransom captives. He clashed with Pope St. Leo over his authority in Gaul but is honored for his holy life.
s360.intercession: St. Hilary of Arles, pray for us. Help us to value people above possessions. Amen.
